'''William Anthony Granville''' (December 16, 1863 – February 4, 1943) was an American mathematician, and served as president of [[Gettysburg College]] from 1910 until 1923.

==Early life==
William Anthony Granville was born on December 16, 1863, in [[White Rock, Minnesota]], to Hannah (née Olson) and T. Pearson Granville. He was of Swedish heritage. He attended [[Gustavus Adolphus College]] and the [[Sheffield Scientific School]] at [[Yale College]].<ref name="obit2">{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-gettysburg-times-dr-granville-pres/173722196/ |title=Dr. Granville, President of Gettysburg 13 Yrs., Dies at 79 |date=1943-02-05 |newspaper=The Gettysburg Times |page=1 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-02}}{{Open access}}</ref> In 1893 he was awarded a bachelor's degree in mathematics from Yale.{{citation needed |date=June 2025}} In 1897, he graduated from Yale with a [[Doctor of Philosophy]].<ref name="obit2"/> He studied under [[James Pierpont (mathematician)|James Pierpont]] and his dissertation was titled, "Referat on the Origin and Development of the Addition-Theorem in Elliptic Functions".{{citation needed |date=June 2025}} He later graduated from [[Lafayette College]] with a [[Doctor of Laws]] in 1911.<ref name="obit2"/> He also attended [[Muhlenberg College]].<ref name="obit3">{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-evening-news-former-head-of-gettysbu/173724174/ |title=Former Head of Gettysburg Dies |date=1943-02-05 |newspaper=The Evening News |page=19 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-03}}{{Open access}}</ref>

==Career==
Granville began his teaching career at [[Bethany College (West Virginia)|Bethany College]], where he was an instructor of mathematics and served as the college treasurer.{{citation needed |date=June 2025}} He was acting president of [[Bethany College (West Virginia)|Bethany College]].<ref name="prexy">{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-gettysburg-times-first-war-prexy-an/173722855/ |title=First War Prexy An Able Educator |date=1943-09-22 |newspaper=The Gettysburg Times |page=13 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-02}}{{Open access}}</ref> He was professor of mathematics at Yale from 1895 to 1910.<ref name="obit"/> He then served as president of [[Gettysburg College]] from October 1910 to 1923.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-patriot-news-new-head-of-gettysburg/173724572/ |title=New Head of Gettysburg College Who Will Be Inaugurated Today |date=1910-10-20 |newspaper=The Patriot |page=1 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-03}}{{Open access}}</ref><ref name="obit">{{Cite web |url=http://www.casact.org/pubs/proceed/proceed42/42166.pdf |title=Obituary:William Anthony Granville, 1863–1943 |publisher=Gettysburg College |pages=166–167 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050507180625/http://www.casact.org/pubs/proceed/proceed42/42166.pdf |archive-date=2005-05-07 |url-status=dead}}</ref> During his tenure as president, he is credited with removing the school's existing debt and establishing an endowment fund. The faculty numbers were increased and the Student Christian association building, the academy building (later Huber Hall) and Weidensall Hall were erected.<ref name="obit2"/><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-evening-sun-william-a-granville-is/173724426/ |title=William A. Granville is Fatally Stricken |date=1943-02-05 |newspaper=The Evening Sun |page=7 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-03}}{{Open access}}</ref> The department of engineering was established, which remained until 1939.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-evening-sun-william-a-granville-is/173724324/ |title=William A. Granville is Fatally Stricken |date=1943-02-05 |newspaper=The Evening Sun |page=1 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=2025-06-03}}{{Open access}}</ref> The summer school was established and the entrance requirements of students was raised. During [[World War I]] at the college, he organized a department of military science and tactics and established [[ROTC]] at the school.<ref name="obit2"/><ref name="obit"/> He was also president of the [[American Federation of Lutheran Brotherhoods]] from 1925 to 1929.<ref name="obit"/><ref name="obit3"/> He wrote textbooks on differential and integral calculus, plane and spherical trigonometry and mathematical analysis.<ref name="obit2"/><ref name="obit"/> He was a member of the [[American Mathematical Society]], [[Sigma Chi]] and the [[American Society of Swedish Engineers]].<ref name="obit2"/>

In 1918, Granville was a member of the executive committee of the [[Churches of Christ]].<ref name="prexy"/> He became affiliated with the Washington National Insurance Company of [[Evanston, Illinois]], on March 1, 1923. He became vice president and director and served in those roles until his death.<ref name="obit"/> He also wrote accident and health insurance manuals.<ref name="obit3"/>

==Personal life==
Granville married Ida Irwin of [[McPherson, Kansas]]. They had two daughters, Rachel and Mrs. S. F. Lehman.<ref name="obit2"/><ref name="obit"/>

Granville died of a heart attack on February 4, 1943, at his home in Chicago.<ref name="obit"/>
